methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Pittman-Robinson Swap Gives Parker the Edge
verdict: Parker is the current winner, with the stronger B- grade and slightly better overall, value, and package scores.
summary: This is a close, fit-driven exchange rather than a blockbuster. Andy’s Long dong silvers move Michael Pittman, whose 66.7 package value and 14.3 season average exceed Brian Robinson’s 63.2 value and 11.0 season average, but the return better matches Andy’s four-RB roster and produces the stronger 86 roster-fit score. Parker’s JankMyKowski TilliSemien adds Pittman to a five-WR roster while sending from a five-RB group, making the swap similarly clean on fit. Parker gets the better value side and the B- grade, while Andy’s C+ reflects a reasonable positional reshuffle. The gap is narrow, but King of Dogshit Trades gets to enjoy this one.

sides.analysis: Andy turns Michael Pittman into Brian Robinson, a move that trades away the higher supplied package value—66.7 versus 63.2—and the stronger season average, 14.3 versus 11.0. The appeal is roster fit: Long dong silvers already carry four running backs, including Derrick Henry, De’Von Achane, and Jonathan Taylor, so Robinson adds another option to a deep position group. The model still gives Andy an 86 roster-fit score, but only a 64 lineup-impact score, meaning the transaction looks more like a useful reshuffle than a lineup-changing strike. At 6-8, Andy gets a targeted fit play, but pays a modest value toll.
sides.bestReason: Robinson aligns with Andy’s running-back-heavy roster, supporting the supplied 86 roster-fit score.
sides.biggestRisk: Andy gives up the higher-value player and better season production, while the lineup-impact score remains 64.

Pittman also brings the better season average, 14.3 compared with Robinson’s 11.0, although his recent average is 7.1. Still, for a 7-7 team with CeeDee Lamb and Justin Jefferson, this is a tidy value win—and the Public Enemy’s trade ledger gets another playful footnote.
